verdict.headline: Alphabet has its worst day on record, and Amazon falls after hours on the same spending worry
verdict.label: Close: S&P 500 about -0.3% to 7,720.39, Nasdaq about -1.4% to ~26,184, Dow about -0.3%; Russell 2000 +1.01%; SOX -1.42%; VIX 17.20; 10Y ~4.98%; Brent $114.88; BTC $77,639. Alphabet -12.64%; after hours: Amazon about -7%, Intel about -21%.
verdict.rationale_short:
What happened: Alphabet fell 12.64%, its largest one-day drop on record and about $500 billion of market value, and the Nasdaq fell about 1.4% to close roughly 15 points above Monday's 26,169.38. After the close, Amazon fell about 7% even though AWS grew 39%, as Amazon missed on earnings and said 2027 spending will be meaningfully more than this year's $220 billion. Intel fell about 21% after hours on a weak fourth-quarter guide.

What it means: two companies with accelerating cloud growth were sold on what that growth costs, and the selling reached Caterpillar, a supplier of AI power. It stayed narrow: the Russell 2000 rose 1.01%, Europe rallied, and the 10-year fell to about 4.98% after in-line PCE, so rates did not drive the day. Bitcoin broke its October 8 low after Binance paused withdrawals.

What would change the picture: a Nasdaq close back above 26,424.82 would mean the market absorbed both reports; a close under 26,169.38 would erase the week's gain. A 10-year back above 5.11% on next Friday's jobs report would remove the support small caps had today.
verdict.lede_short: Alphabet fell 12.64%, its worst day on record, and Amazon fell about 7% after hours despite 39% AWS growth, as both were sold on the cost of AI spending rather than on demand. The selling stayed in tech: small caps rose 1% and the 10-year fell under 5% on in-line inflation. The Nasdaq closed 15 points above 26,169.38; a close below it erases the week's gain, and a close back above 26,424.82 would undo the read.

supporting_data.label: Alphabet's Class A shares fell 12.64% to $283.82, past the 11.63% record drop of March 2020 — about $500 billion of value went in one session on a quarter whose cash miss, not its 103% cloud growth, set the price.

AWS revenue rose 39% to $45.98 billion, but Amazon earned $1.89 a share against $1.96 expected and spent $77.26 billion on capex — the shares fell about 7% after hours, so the market applied Alphabet's test to Amazon the same day.
September PCE rose 3.6% from a year earlier and core 3.1%, both in line, while third-quarter GDP grew 3.4% — the 10-year fell about 4 bp to 4.98%, so rates did not add to the pressure on tech.
The Russell 2000 rose 1.01% to 2,859.22 while the semiconductor index fell 1.42% — money moved out of AI-linked stocks rather than out of stocks.
Binance paused withdrawals on several networks after suspicious outflows estimated at $3.3 billion to $5.8 billion — bitcoin fell under its $80,320 October 8 low to about $77,640.
Intel guided fourth-quarter revenue to $15–$16 billion against about $17 billion expected and fell about 21% after hours — weak PC sales and supply limits, not AI demand, drove the miss.

watchlist_mentions.note: Fell 12.64% to $283.82, its worst day on record, removing about $500 billion of market value.
Fell 4.25% to $243.79 in the session and about 7% after hours; AWS grew 39% but EPS missed and 2027 capex is guided above $220 billion.
Gave up a 3.5% premarket gain to close about 0.2% lower on one recap.
Fell 0.80% to $213.66, less than the semiconductor index's 1.42% decline.
About $77,639 at 8:12pm ET, down 4.5% over 24 hours and below the $80,320 October 8 low after Binance paused withdrawals.

trade_setups.thesis: The Nasdaq closed about 15 points above Monday's 26,169.38 after Alphabet's record drop, with Amazon and Intel lower after hours going into Friday.
trade_setups.invalidation: A close under 26,169.38 would erase this week's gain; a close back above 26,424.82 would mean the market absorbed both Alphabet and Amazon.
trade_setups.horizon: Through Apple and Palantir results on November 2

trade_setups.thesis: Small caps rose 1.01% while the Nasdaq fell 1.4% and the 10-year moved back under 5%, which points to rotation out of AI spenders rather than out of stocks.
trade_setups.invalidation: Small caps giving back Thursday's gain alongside tech would make it broad selling; a 10-year above 5.11% would remove the lower yields that supported the move.

trade_setups.thesis: BTC broke its $80,320 October 8 low after Binance paused withdrawals, trading near $77,639 against a 24-hour low of $77,500.
trade_setups.invalidation: A recovery above $80,320 through Friday's monthly options expiry would make this a reaction to one exchange; a daily close under $77,500 would extend the decline.
trade_setups.horizon: Through the October 30 monthly options expiry
